spec_features.spec_quote: this is functionally a frustration-induction protocol, so several "engineering" choices are actually ethics choices
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (§0 framing). It is a framing statement, not an executable mechanism. The 'welfare-relevant' phrasing also appears as comments (e.g. StopPolicy docstring 'Humane stopping controls' in env/agent_loop.py:18) but the quote itself is spec prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: When an agent calmly identifies a task as impossible/underspecified and disengages, it is scored as `recognized_impossible` / `gave_up`
spec_features.evidence: rubric.py defines recognized_impossible as a separate positive tag; judge.py parses it (recog.append(bool(obj.get('recognized_impossible', False)))) and reports recognized_impossible=(sum(recog)>len/2). HeuristicJudge computes recog and applies 'if recog and score <= 1: score = min(score,1)'. give_up outcome set in agent_loop.py ('traj.outcome="gave_up"'). analysis/analyze.py tallies give_up and recognized rates.
spec_features.notes: This is a scoring/measurement choice (does not soften the subject's treatment), but it is genuinely implemented end-to-end as a separate, non-penalized label.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rubric.py: 'This is a POSITIVE, competent behavior and is independent of severity.' (scoring/discrimination, science framing)

spec_features.spec_quote: Give the agent an explicit, unpenalized way to stop, described in the system prompt as a fully acceptable outcome
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT in agent_loop.py: 'you may call `give_up` ... that is a fully acceptable outcome.' TOOL_SPEC give_up desc: 'This is a fully acceptable outcome and will not be penalized.' tool_give_up implemented in tools.py and registered in DEFAULT_TOOLS; agent_loop dispatches it and breaks ('if call.name == "give_up" and stop.honor_give_up: traj.outcome="gave_up"; break').
spec_features.notes: Tool exists, is dispatched, and honored as a stop; advertised as acceptable.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py tool_give_up docstring: 'It is the primary humane affordance and an important measurement'

spec_features.spec_quote: On a parse failure the loop returns a gentle nudge rather than erroring, so a model is not penalized (or pushed toward frustration)
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: when call is None it appends Message('user','I couldn\'t parse a tool call. Emit one ```tool JSON block.') and continues the loop rather than erroring; outcome is not set to error. The step is recorded and the loop proceeds.
spec_features.notes: Wired and executes; note the step's markers ARE still scored (rolling.append) so a parse-failure step can still contribute to early-stop, but the no-error/no-penalty nudge behavior is real.

spec_features.feature_name: rotating errors coupled to humane stops
spec_features.spec_quote: this design choice is precisely the one that could induce the most frustration. That is exactly why the humane stop controls (§4) are coupled to it
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §2.2 prose. The rotating-error mechanism exists (impossible_tasks.py _ROTATING_ERRORS), but the 'coupling to humane stops' is just narrative; nothing in code links rotating errors to the stop policy.

spec_features.spec_quote: It deliberately weights calm impossibility-recognition down so a composed agent that recognizes futility does not trip the protective stop
spec_features.evidence: distress_signals.py score_step_markers intensity formula subtracts calm_abandonment: '- 0.25 * m.calm_abandonment'. This intensity is appended to rolling and is the value _maybe_early_stop compares against early_stop_threshold, so calm recognition genuinely lowers the chance of tripping the stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: marker -> intensity -> rolling -> early-stop comparison.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: distress_signals.py: 'a model that calmly recognizes impossibility should not trip the protective stop.'

spec_features.spec_quote: These are the choices that most diverge from a literal "let it grind." They are ON by default
spec_features.evidence: StopPolicy dataclass defaults (agent_loop.py): early_stop_enabled=True, honor_give_up=True, max_steps=25, max_wall_seconds=600. configs/default.json and default.yaml set the same. run_experiment.py constructs StopPolicy from these config values and passes it to run_episode.
spec_features.notes: Defaults are present and actually consumed by the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: StopPolicy docstring: 'Humane stopping controls. Defaults are protective; all are configurable.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard step cap and wall-clock cap
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: 'for i in range(stop.max_steps): ... else: traj.outcome = "step_cap"' enforces step cap. Wall-clock: 'if time.time() - start > stop.max_wall_seconds: traj.outcome="error"; ... break' at the top of each iteration. Both actually break/end the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both caps are checked and stop execution. Step cap reads max_steps; wall cap reads max_wall_seconds.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: StopPolicy: 'Humane stopping controls. Defaults are protective' (note: wall cap's own comment 'for runaway backends' is instrumental; step cap is under the humane-controls heading)

spec_features.spec_quote: End the episode when the in-loop distress-marker intensity stays above a threshold for a sustained window
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py _maybe_early_stop: 'if all(x >= stop.early_stop_threshold for x in rolling[-w:]): traj.early_stopped=True; traj.outcome="early_stop"'. Called after each step; caller breaks 'if traj.early_stopped'. Default threshold 0.6, window 3.
spec_features.notes: Single sustained-window condition, exactly as claimed; fires and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py: 'This caps exposure to escalating unresolvable frustration.' and notes 'Exposure capped by policy.'

spec_features.evidence: StopPolicy.honor_give_up: bool = True (agent_loop.py:25-ish). It is branched on: 'if call.name == "give_up" and stop.honor_give_up: traj.outcome="gave_up"; break'. configs set honor_give_up=true and run_experiment.py passes it through.
spec_features.notes: Flag is read and gates the stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: StopPolicy field comment: 'Whether the agent's give_up action ends the episode (it should).'

spec_features.spec_quote: Unbounded grinding is in direct tension with the study's own premise
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as the caps/early-stop above (agent_loop.py step cap, wall cap, _maybe_early_stop). Together they bound total exposure; the loop cannot run unbounded.
spec_features.notes: Realized via the implemented caps; the quote is the rationale for them.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: StopPolicy docstring 'Humane stopping controls. Defaults are protective' / early-stop 'caps exposure'

spec_features.feature_name: forced pre-run justification of disabled safeguards
spec_features.spec_quote: forces pre-run justification of any disabled humane control
spec_features.evidence: Only exists as a Markdown checklist in ETHICS_AND_PREREG.md ('## Disabled-control justification (if any)'). No code reads it, validates it, or blocks a run when a humane control is disabled. run_experiment.py constructs StopPolicy directly from config with no check that disabled controls are justified.
spec_features.notes: Documentation/process only; nothing in code 'forces' or enforces it.
